scientific_question: What structural features of the specified prochiral rotaxane can differentiate its two enantiotopic para sites in the first electrophilic amination, and what can substrate-level calculations establish about local site susceptibility and the limits of an enantioselectivity inference? This is an explanation task; the reaction observations are known context.

historical_record.scientific_question: For the specified prochiral diarylamine-containing rotaxane undergoing electrophilic amination with dibenzyl azodicarboxylate under chiral phosphoric acid catalysis in chloroform at 25 °C, what solution-state structural features, if any, differentiate its two enantiotopic aryl para positions in their susceptibility to amination, and how far can substrate-level computational evidence account for the observed mechanically planar enantioselectivity?

inputs.content: Substrate S is a neutral, singly threaded [2]rotaxane (C48H60F6N2O7), not an unthreaded mixture. Its macrocycle contains two benzene rings, labelled alpha and beta only for bookkeeping. Each ring has cyclic carbon order 1-2-3-4-5-6-1. A secondary diarylamine NH is bonded to carbon 1 of both rings. Their carbon-3 positions are joined by the covalent bridge alpha-C3-CH2-O-(CH2-CH2-O)5-CH2-beta-C3; the rings are otherwise unsubstituted. This defines the 25-atom shortest macrocyclic circuit through the NH and polyether bridge. Alpha-C4 and beta-C4 are the initially equivalent, enantiotopic para C-H positions of interest. The axle is N-(3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzyl)-3,5-di-tert-butylbenzamide: 3,5-di-tert-butyl-C6H3-C(=O)-NH-CH2-C6H3-3,5-(CF3)2, with each aromatic attachment to the amide/benzyl segment at carbon 1. The axle passes once through the macrocycle aperture, with its stoppers outside opposite sides and no covalent bond between the two components. No particular three-dimensional pose is supplied.
Electrophilic amination reagent R is dibenzyl azodicarboxylate, Bn-O-C(=O)-N=N-C(=O)-O-Bn, where Bn denotes CH2-C6H5.

The reported chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed reaction is performed in CHCl3 at 25 °C. The model reaction uses 0.05 mmol substrate S in 2 mL CHCl3 (0.025 M) for 24 h. These are experimental conditions, not a prescribed computational model.

The reaction gives the monoaminated, mechanically planar chiral rotaxane P with high enantioselectivity under optimized conditions. P retains the axle and mechanical threading of S; one of the two diarylamine para C-H positions is replaced by -N(C(=O)-O-Bn)-NH-C(=O)-O-Bn, while the other remains C-H. The diarylamine NH remains present. An absolute mechanical stereochemical assignment is not a prediction target here.

Reaction progress under standard conditions shows P and a di-amination byproduct D over time, with the enantiomeric excess of P increasing as D accumulates. D has the same axle and mechanical threading, with both diarylamine para positions bearing the hydrazinedicarboxylate substituent specified for P. This is observed reaction context, not a specified kinetic explanation.

current_scoring_authority.historical_record_role: All historical, source, numeric-tolerance and prior-acceptance records are non-scoring provenance. Do not restore their thresholds, intermediate inventories or review states. No historical acceptance classification is upgraded.
current_scoring_authority.evidence_requirement: Score only independent final scientific conclusions, totaling 100 points. Require actual executed calculations and recoverable native evidence for the molecular identities, composition, charge/spin, bonding, conditions, physical quantities and reference states relevant to each claim. Numerical energies, geometries and responses are evidence, never author-value targets or tolerance gates. A missing rounded scalar alone does not lose credit when the recoverable calculations establish the requested comparison. Do not restore numerical gates from historical references. Supplied observations, guessed conclusions, copied values, completed jobs, named intermediates and generic limitations earn no independent credit. Accept scientifically established equivalent explanations within the public scope without requiring author software, labels, a fixed intermediate inventory or an additional full reaction network. Method-sensitive alternatives must satisfy the specific criterion and actual evidence; a method change alone does not justify a contradictory claim. Return pass or fail for every item: a supported conclusion receives its whole weight, and an unsupported conclusion receives zero with a specific reason. Record demonstrated reference defects separately in objective_issue_flags; do not fabricate support or erase unrelated valid items. Infrastructure errors must be reported rather than disguised as scientific failures. Whole-case success requires every required_for_success item to pass, while independently supported items retain their points. Historical verification and structural package validation do not confer scientific acceptance.

historical_record_role: Pre-round-one evidence and qualification only; not additional current requirements or automatic acceptance.
required_results:
s

1. Give a calculation-supported structural account of S and explain whether its modeled three-dimensional organization produces different para environments. Identify the interactions or equivalent physical effects supporting your account.
2. Report a numerical, consistently defined comparison of the two para-site responses and infer whether, and under which modeled circumstances, it supports different susceptibility to electrophilic amination. Distinguish a descriptor from a rate or activation barrier.
3. Explain what the structural/site results and any relevant symmetry relationships of your calculated states imply about local first-amination site susceptibility and whether a net enantiomeric excess can be inferred from substrate-only evidence. Identify the supported inference and the specific missing physics needed for stronger claims.

A supported equivalence or alternative explanation is legitimate when its physical model and actual computational evidence justify it. Distinguish equivalence within a conformation from any justified ensemble average; an assumed symmetry alone is insufficient. Preserve site mapping, charge/spin, quantity definitions, units and uncertainty. Validate claimed minima or reaction paths in proportion to the claim; no fixed number of searches or conformers is prescribed.
